clue.text: Both parents collect a new hat

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so the parents hold the other letters between them

parts.note: the two parents are PA and MA, written together

explanation.surface: Mother and father club together to buy a fresh hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The parents' letters stand together and take in N then A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight brimmed straw hat, a specific example of headwear.

clue.text: Local tour that goes swimmingly?

parts.note: a local is a British pub, so a tour of locals is a drinking round; the crawl is also a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood outing that runs very smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's nearby pub; 'crawl' doubles as the front swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is an evening drinking at several bars in turn.

clue.text: Americans are from a different planet

parts.note: new means different, as in a new start
a world is a planet

explanation.surface: A jibe that people from the USA are like aliens.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls 'Men are from Mars'; the definition is the place Americans come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Europeans named the Americas after Columbus's voyages the newly found half of the globe.

clue.text: Hearing revolutionary, takes notice

indicators.note: said aloud to a listener, so the revolutionary's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Karl Marx, the revolutionary thinker

explanation.surface: A radical at a trial pays attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session, but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to observe or heed it, as in 'mark my words'.

clue.text: Tackling Alp, hasn't a walking stick

indicators.note: tackling a job means working at it and knocking it into shape, so these letters get reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A climber setting out on an Alpine peak has forgotten a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackling' reads as the climber's effort, but it signals that ALP and HASNT are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashplant is a sapling of ash cut and used as a cane for walkers.

clue.text: Random glances around from muck spreader

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone looks about idly from a farm vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Random' seems an anagram signal but is fodder; 'around' rearranges both words. 'Muck spreader' sounds agricultural but means a gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandalmonger spreads malicious gossip, and muck is a slang word for dirt or scandal.

clue.text: Burning desire

parts.note: usually a strong longing, but literally an urge to set fires

explanation.surface: An intense longing for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsion to start fires, so literally a craving to burn things.

clue.text: Sailor given errand is away

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
one given an errand is sent off on it

explanation.surface: A seaman is sent off on a task and so is not around.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, gone elsewhere.

clue.text: Examiner is in wrong street

indicators.note: the street's letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An inspector has got lost in the wrong road.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester checks or tries things out, as an examiner does.

clue.text: Violinist's private room

definitions.meaning: a violinist plays with a bow, so is one who bows
a lady's private chamber or a shady garden retreat

explanation.surface: A musician's own little practice room.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is read as one who bows, rhyming with 'lower', not 'flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is an old word for a secluded chamber, and also literally someone who wields a bow.

clue.text: Chief relaxes car safety features

parts.note: head means chief, as in head teacher
rests means relaxes

explanation.surface: The boss takes it easy among the protective fittings of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Headrests are padded supports atop vehicle seats that protect the neck in a collision.

clue.text: Famous person's family title

definitions.note: someone so well known everyone recognises them

parts.note: a household is a family living together
a name is a title

explanation.surface: A celebrity's surname as their clan's label.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a celebrity so widely known they are familiar in every home.

clue.text: Police team having wildly exciting time?

definitions.text: Police team having wildly exciting time?

parts.words: Police team having wildly exciting time?
parts.note: a riot is a wildly exciting time, so a squad having one would be a team in that state; really it is a unit sent to quell public disorder

explanation.surface: Officers letting their hair down at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'riot' as great fun; the real unit deals with the other kind of riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot squad is a body of officers trained to control violent crowds and disorder.

clue.text: A fine cut of meat

parts.note: looks like praise for a quality joint, but it means meat that has been chopped finely

explanation.surface: A butcher praises a choice joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' seems to mean excellent, but it means small: the meat is cut into tiny pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince is ground or finely chopped meat, called ground beef in America.

clue.text: On board ship, head for the drink

definitions.text: On board ship, head for the drink

parts.words: On board ship, head for the drink
parts.note: sounds like a sailor going to the bar, but it is a pirate victim forced along a board into the sea, 'the drink'

explanation.surface: A sailor goes off to find something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, and the 'board' is the plank itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates made captives step off a board over the side, sending them into the ocean.

clue.text: Incredible account of the giraffe?

definitions.meaning: a story told about a lofty animal would be a high one

explanation.surface: An unbelievable yarn about a long-necked animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: a giraffe's story would be tall like the giraffe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an exaggerated tale hard to believe.

clue.text: Start making dress from pattern and stop

definitions.meaning: the first step in dressmaking is to snip the shape out of a paper pattern
an informal order to quit doing something

explanation.surface: A dressmaker is told to begin, then to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressmakers first snip shapes out of a paper template; the same phrase is an idiom ordering someone to quit.

clue.text: Strong, virile types submitted to surgeon

indicators.note: the virile types are submitted to, or put into the hands of, the surgeon, ending up inside his letters

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
he-men are macho, virile men

explanation.surface: Macho men go under the knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submitted to' reads as yielding, but it signals going inside; 'surgeon' means an animal doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful or intense in feeling.

clue.text: The opposite of what AA stands for?

definitions.text: The opposite of what AA stands for?

parts.words: The opposite of what AA stands for?
parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, which stands for sobriety; the reverse of that cause is excessive drinking, and the phrase plays on the letters AA

explanation.surface: A question about the values a well-known organisation upholds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands for' suggests expanding the initials; it means what the group supports. The answer's two words also begin with A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholics Anonymous campaigns against problem drinking, so its opposite is the misuse of liquor.

clue.text: Casually read book, gets worse in translation

indicators.note: translating changes the form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A novel suffers when put into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to skim a text in a leisurely way.

clue.text: Drinking vessel allowed to touch mouth

indicators.note: the allowed word is placed so it touches the mouth, right beside it

parts.note: gob is British slang for mouth
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A cup is permitted to come up to the lips.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is British slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a stemmed wine glass or cup.

clue.text: Firmly establishes ancestry

definitions.meaning: a verb: to fix something deeply in place, as a plant does

explanation.surface: Someone settles a question of family descent.
explanation.definitionFit: To root a plant is to fix it firmly in soil, and one's family origins are figuratively where one grew from.

clue.text: Biscuit gives diet variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version or form, so these letters appear in another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cookie adds some interest to a dull eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks like a noun about food, but it rearranges GIVES DIET.
explanation.definitionFit: A digestive is a semi-sweet British wholemeal biscuit, much like a Graham cracker.

clue.text: Walk furtively in square with nothing to do

parts.note: S is short for square, as in street names
idle means unoccupied

explanation.surface: A bored loiterer slinks about the town square.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move sideways or stealthily.

clue.text: Be elated to have one's stroll broadcast?

definitions.note: an idiom for feeling joyful, as if floating

parts.note: a walk is a stroll
on air means being broadcast

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at their walk being transmitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have one's' links the two parts; 'on air' is broadcasting jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A set idiom for being so joyful one seems to float.

clue.text: Perhaps bee managed to cross river

indicators.note: to cross something is to go across its middle, so the river letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: done means managed, as in got done
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An insect contrives to fly over a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks that a male bee is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male honeybee; 'perhaps' shows bee is one example, the word also meaning a remote aircraft.

clue.text: Charge through the gate

parts.note: sounds like rushing past a barrier, but means a fee paid at a gate to be admitted

explanation.surface: A bull or crowd storms through an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a violent rush; it is a price, the gate being a turnstile.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission price paid at the entrance to an event or attraction.

clue.text: Go away and get busy

definitions.meaning: read as three words, to ... means to be busily working

explanation.surface: A boss tells an idler to leave or start working.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for clearing off, and split into three words it gives 'be at it', meaning to work hard.
